edge_cases: Missing required JSON fields in /add_book or /update_book may cause a server error
Providing a non‑existent book_id to update or delete returns success message but affects no rows
Empty keyword or genre parameters return all rows (or none) depending on the query
SQL injection is possible because user input is interpolated directly into queries
Database errors (e.g., table missing) result in a 500 internal server error
Large request bodies or result sets may exceed default Flask limits
contract.intent: Expose a RESTful HTTP API that lets clients add, search, update, delete, and list books in an SQLite‑backed library database.
invariants: Each book row has columns id (primary key), title, author, genre
All responses are JSON‑encoded and include an HTTP status code
Database file name is fixed as library.db
Connection is closed after each request regardless of success
The API does not perform authentication or authorization
io_behavior: POST /add_book with JSON {title, author, genre} → 201 and JSON {"message":"Book added successfully"}
GET /search_books?keyword=… → 200 and JSON array of matching rows (title or author contains keyword)
PUT /update_book/<book_id> with JSON {title?, author?, genre?} → 200 and JSON {"message":"Book updated successfully"}
GET /get_books_by_genre?genre=… → 200 and JSON array of rows whose genre equals the parameter
side_effects: Inserts a new row into the books table
Updates an existing row identified by its id
Deletes a row identified by its id
Commits the transaction to persist changes in library.db
Opens and closes a SQLite connection for each request

rationale: The program implements the required routes and returns JSON with correct status codes, preserving most invariants and side‑effects. However, it deviates from the contract on update_book (requires all fields instead of optional) and get_books_by_genre (rejects missing genre instead of returning all/none). It also mitigates the expected SQL‑injection vulnerability, contrary to the contract's edge‑case description. These mismatches lower the behavior, I/O semantics, and edge‑case scores.
